My review of Elden Ring After 100 hours!!! And after completing the game 100% I can say it’s not just a game — it’s a legendary masterpiece! At the very least, it’s a complete game. A world with this level of beauty, scale, depth, and visual variety — from lush, green natural lands to desert regions and volcanic areas, from snowy realms and dragon-infested worlds to even an underground world. From the moment you enter the game, you realize you’re standing before the greatest game of the century — perhaps even the greatest thing ever created in gaming. The world design is carefully crafted and precise, but nothing surpasses the mastery and precision of the boss fights. Literally, Souls games are the only ones that have perfected boss combat — where you must memorize the boss’s moves, learn their fighting style, and master dodging with the correct timing. And since we mentioned timing, how can we not bring up parrying with shields — a unique and excellent feature in Souls / Souls-like games. The story has a depth that pulls you into deep thought, and the soundtracks transport you to another world, making the experience even more incredible. The variety of weapons — from magic, swords, bows, and spears — along with the diversity of skills (Ashes of War), adds even more richness. By the way, the game isn’t primarily based on magic, yet it contains hundreds of spells — meaning it even surpasses games that are built around magic, like Hogwarts Legacy. I don’t even know how to describe the greatness of the bosses to you. You’ll face some of the greatest bosses in Souls games — I’m talking about General Radahn, the Starscourge, descendant of war, the Red Lion, breaker of kings, shedder of blood. And I’m talking about Malenia, Lady of the Sword, the undefeated Blade of Miquella, the lone flower of the Elden. And not to mention Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, warrior of kings, breaker of thrones, the White Lion, the embodiment of raw power. The game is difficult and gives you nothing easily, but it rewards every effort you put in and every skill you learn. Every step is calculated, every decision carries weight, every moment is full of excitement, and every minute you spend in the game is a unique experience. Elden Ring is the crown of gaming. It doesn’t just deserve Game of the Year — it deserves Game of the Century. They made this masterpiece in just 5 years, which is honestly insane. Even the biggest studios couldn’t pull off something like this in that time. And yeah, I don’t regret spending a single penny on this game. Thanks, FromSoftware.

This game feels like it’s written by an adult who proved to their parents that “it’s not just a phase!” and never grew out of the edgy teenager persona they had in the early 2000s. Every time your character opens their mouth they sound like they’re trying to sound cool, but they come across so cringe worthy instead. Even after an NPC you’ve met a couple times commits suicide and you’re helping their friend afterwards and you’re about to leave, your character goes “holler on the holo (phone) if you need anything”. Even in that moment you’d character doesn’t show any genuine emotion or concern. “If you need anything at all, I’m here for you!” would not have been cool enough for this game… jfc Don’t get me started on Keanu Reeves character. He is insanely childish and “edgy”. He is exhausting! Which is sad because Keanu seems like a genuinely great person irl. And then there are the car chases where you’re a passenger. They’re the least convincing car chases I’ve ever seen! A child playing with car toys makes more convincing chases. And that’s what it feels like, a child holding the car and moving it around. There’s no hint of physics at all. Like sure, you have to put the car on rails to make the sequence work the way you want, but at least make it feel realistic. Don’t jerk the car around like a toddler and ignore the terrain under it. The only thing I like about the game so far is the graphics and atmosphere. With ray tracing on it looks amazing and it’s fun to walk around and look at it. That’s about it though for me.

A very satisfying gaming experience. If you are a casual and having difficulty at first, use the God Mode which gives you an incremental increase in percent resistance to damage each time you die. As you keep trying and dying, you will get better and learn what is needed to be done with each of the available weapons to complete a run to the end. To complete a run and defeat Hades is quite enjoyable and it all revolves around an interesting story involving the Gods of Antiquity. One has to complete a total of 10 runs, in order to complete the story line aspect of the game. But the game is really designed to allow for a lot more gameplay afterwards offering a number of ways to vary the challenge.

[h2] Hades Review 2026 [/h2] [h3]Gameplay[/h3] [b]9[/b] There were very few moments where I didn't feel like completing a run because even if I got crappy boons, it was fun to see if I could progress. All the weapons are very unique and completely change the way you play. The progression system has you reaching max talents to help you make it through the encounters by around 30 hours and then after that you're working on learning the synergies between gods and planning out builds, which is daunting at first but becomes enjoyable. [h3]Story[/h3] [b]10[/b] It's very good. Took me nearly 50 hours before I heard a repeated dialogue line. I gotta know how much they paid their voice actors because it probably isn't enough. [h3]Sound/Atmosphere[/h3] [b]10[/b] Again, it's perfect. All the sound effects and voice actors are amazing. Maybe not hypnos, but the others are so good that it's still a 10. [h3]Music[/h3] [b]10[/b] I want to meet the bass player and shake his hand. [h3]Replayability[/h3] [b]10[/b] I never felt like it was a chore to play this game while I was hunting achievements. Will definitely play again in the future.

I've played Elden Ring more times than I can count, first on PS4 when it launched, then again on PS5, and came back once more when Shadow of the Erdtree dropped, and now on PC, every single run, it still finds a way to impress, the gameplay is the foundation everything else sits on, and FromSoftware absolutely nailed it. The level design is masterful, each region has its own identity and mood, and legacy dungeons like Stormveil and Leyndell are some of the most carefully crafted spaces I've ever explored in a game. The cutscenes are genuinely stunning, the art, the lighting, the scale and the Soundtracks ofc. If you want to start a FromSoftware game, Elden Ring is your go-to, It's far more beginner friendly than people make it out to be, yes there are hard parts, but the summon system is there for a reason, struggling with a boss? Call for help, It genuinely makes the experience more accessible without taking anything away from it. And the DLC, At 40€ Shadow of the Erdtree is a steal, the amount of content, new areas, new weapons, and bosses it brings closer to a full sequel than an expansion, If you loved the base game, this is non-negotiable.

Forza Horizon 5 is easily the best open-world racer out there. The map’s massive, the car roster is wild, and the driving feels great — whether you're tearing through dirt, hitting high-speed highways, or dialing in smooth drifts. Compared to The Crew 2, it handles way better. NFS Unbound has style, but Forza has variety — street races, off-road, drift zones, speed traps, stunts, seasonal events... there's always something to do. It's just pure, fun driving with no grindy nonsense.
